Well, I am in the market for this, done hours of research and still behind on the game. I am an amateur, skilled photographer, looking to make a creative foray into short film making. Please feel free to add or disagree, or call me a pinhead, I don't care. Just need input from more experienced people out there. Here's what I learned so far:

1) Canons, while good for filmmaking, are overpriced in the new market. Canon fx and dx frame new cameras are probably overpriced by about 30 percent compared to Nikon, arguably a better camera for stills and can match canons for video, at least starting at the mid range level. I am wondering if this is because canon hates their consumers. There doesn't seem to be any business sense for this.

2) Great deals to be had in used Canon market. My local craigslist has a T5i for 350. Huge assortment of quality lenses for good price. Just getting a cheap body opens doors for having money left over for spending on lenses and other cool stuff. Canon is the way to go if you choose to buy used. With magic lantern, these cheaper used cameras become great, with options to directly set kelvin, ect.

3) Nikons have a disadvantage compared to Canons due to lack of peak focusing feature. This could impact filmmaking/video? Trying to manually pull focus on a moving subject can be a pain, it seems to me that peak focusing feature would really help with that. I guess this doesn't matter if you plan on just taking stills. Also, nikon lenses are more expensive. Nikons also don't allow changing of aperature during live video, I doubt that is much of a problem though. If you plan on film making you should have these things thought out ahead of time. The lack of peak focus can be a deal breaker though.

4) 4K.... Is it really all that important? It seems to be a good way to increase your expense since you have to add new computers and hard drives to deal with the increased data. Most people aren't going to look at your film or stills on anything but a computer monitor anyway. Seems to be an overrated feature. I can see needing this if you make commercials or something for companies who will advertise on these HD TV's. It's probably not necessary for amateur, indy film makers and photographers.

5) Mirrorless cameras. I think they are overrated, or at least that is the impression I am getting. I found something interesting in google. If you do a search for mirrorless vs dslr you will pull up tons of articles from 5-10 years ago on popular science and tech/photo people telling you what a dickhead you would be to invest in a dslr, and not mirrorless. Yet here we are today, and dslr's are still with us, cheap and popular as ever. Why should I invest in mirrorless? Not convinced they offer any advantage except a smaller body. Yet, most of them give a smaller sensor and higher price. Especially when there are tons of great used cheap canons to be bought that will give a bigger sensor and a nice selection of lenses.

6) Flip screen. You really need this for video. Canon has it, Nikon doesn't unless you get their high end expensive cameras.

7) Does a full frame sensor offer any advantage at all for video over a smaller sensor (like APS-C)? I am still trying to figure this one out. I can definitely see the advantage for low light and being able to get closer to subject, so it seems to me the answer is yes. The question is does this advantage apply to video/filmmaking as well? I understand full frame cameras are much more expensive though.

8) Here's a good thing I learned. Most of the camera conventions/expos by makers happen at the end of year and beginning of year. After which they bring new cameras onto the market, the price drops considerably on older models. That means that the best time to buy a camera is around March which is coming right up! Gives me plenty of time to keep researching and learning.

It seems to me that a lower end used Canon like T5i is with magic lantern installed is the way to go for hybrid camera that will allow you to make indie films and do still photography. All things considered. Anyone disagree with this? Unless you absolutely insist on full frame. Again, does anyone have any input on the FX (full frame) vs DX and smaller sensors? Is it worth paying more to get this?

Thanks!
